answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with burn-to-register identity: creating an identity requires destroying a small fee, like nectar paid to enter a garden, and the receipt is public. One fake account costs little, but a farm of ten thousand must burn ten thousand fees, with no refund when caught. Fees also rise on a ledge: the more identities funded from one wallet cluster, the higher each next registration costs. A saffron harvest is rare and costly to fake at scale; the same logic makes bulk fakery ruinous while one honest agent stays cheap.
